title: The 'Made in India' Stamp That Ended Ardeshir Godrej's Scalpels
conflicts: Purpose of Cama's 3,000-rupee loan: surgical instruments (company history, Wikipedia) versus the lock business (The Better India); the story ties it only to the instruments. Springless-lock patent: July 1908 (company) versus 1909 (Business Today); the story says 'within about a dozen years'. The 'Made in India' stamp rests on the company history and Wikipedia (both from Karanjia's authorised biography); The Better India says only the venture 'did not do well', and The Week (unreadable here) reportedly gives a 'Made in England' variant; the story attributes the stamp to the company's account. The company's 'forty steam presses' in a 20 m² shed is omitted as implausible.
notes: Quote stance: affirms. Independent sourcing for the stamp dispute is thinner than for the rest; the editor may want to weigh that. Wikipedia used once, supplementary. Business Standard (1998) and The Week (2023) could not be read and are not cited.
